expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: type Subscription = SubscriptionBase & (| { status: "trialing"; ... } | { status: "active"; ... } | ...) — status discriminates

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: canceled variant has only status, canceledAt, and cancellation; trialing has only status and trialEndsAt

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: function assertNever(x: never) with default: return assertNever(sub) in switch

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionId and CustomerId are branded types using Brand<T, B> pattern

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Provides function signature canTransition(...): boolean but implementation throws 'not yet defined' — no actual constraint

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Discusses preventing nonsense states, explains nested CancellationReason union prevents 'voluntary: true + payment_failed', names ID swap prevention, branding benefits

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Misuse section item 1 rejects bag allowing 'active + retryCount: 3'
